claim:
In the basic Feynman-checker model of Skopenkov and Ustinov, let \(a=a_1+i a_2\), and for \(0<v<1\) define
\[
G_t(v)=\frac{2}{t}\sum_{\substack{0\le x\le vt\\x+t\ \mathrm{even}}}\left|\frac{a_2(x,t)}{a(x,t)}\right|^2.
\]
Then \(G_t(v)\to G(v)\) for every \(0<v<1\). With \(v_*=1/\sqrt2\),
\[
G(v)=\frac14\left(1+2v-\sqrt{1-2v^2}+\log\frac{1+\sqrt{1-2v^2}}2\right),\qquad 0<v<v_*,
\]
and
\[
G(v)=\frac14+\frac v2+\frac14\left(\log\frac{v}{\sqrt2}+\sqrt{2v^2-1}-\arctan\sqrt{2v^2-1}\right),\qquad v_*<v<1.
\]
The two branches meet with
\[
G(v_*)=\frac{1+\sqrt2-\log2}{4},\qquad G'(v_*^-)=G'(v_*^+)=\frac{2+\sqrt2}{4},
\]
and
\[
G(v)=G(v_*)+\frac{2+\sqrt2}{4}(v-v_*)+\frac{2^{1/4}}3|v-v_*|^{3/2}+O((v-v_*)^2).
\]
Hence \(G\) is \(C^1\) but not \(C^2\) at the wall. In particular, the formula proposed in Problem 4 of the cited source for \(0<v<1/\sqrt2\) is false: it contains \(\sqrt{1-v^2}\) where the actual phase-averaged law produces \(\sqrt{1-2v^2}\). The second displayed branch gives the previously requested hidden-region value.
integrity: The proof separates published asymptotic inputs from the new phase average, adjacent-site large-deviation ratio, integration, and wall expansion. No independent validation or publication claim is asserted.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to the basic unit-step, unit-mass Feynman checker and fixed positive velocities.
No uniform convergence rate through the wall is claimed; the wall is crossed by compact-region asymptotics plus the bound that every conditional probability lies in [0,1].
Finite recurrence calculations are corroborative and are not used to infer the infinite-time limit.
An equivalent calculation may exist in unindexed literature under local-chirality terminology.
title: Corrected conditional endpoint law for the Feynman checker
